approved: Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting Shackling During Childbirth) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would ban the practice of restraining people while they give birth.
It would insert a new section into the Crimes Act 1914 that prohibits shackling during childbirth and overrides any inconsistent state or territory laws.
The ban would start the day after the bill receives royal assent.
The bill prohibits the restraint of people during childbirth.
The bill overrides any state or territory law that conflicts with the new prohibition.
The bill applies the ban to conduct in Commonwealth places and territories.
People giving birth in Australian jurisdictions, including in Commonwealth places and territories.

Moved the Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting Shackling During Childbirth) Bill 2026 for second reading, arguing that shackling during childbirth is unnecessary, dangerous, medically harmful, degrading and inconsistent with human rights obligations. The explanatory memorandum was tabled, leave was granted to incorporate the speech in Hansard, and debate was adjourned.
